source.notes: Paper prints: Series P1QSR, 'SET~1' (text layer; stored as SET-1), Q.P. Code 57/1/1, 23 printed pages (24 PDF pages including covers), 33 questions, Maximum Marks 70, Time allowed 3 hours. Session is not printed on the paper. English text is on odd PDF pages (Hindi on even pages). This was the first Q.P. code in the archive (57/1/1) with a matching English marking-scheme section and a clean, usable text layer; pdftotext reports many 'Missing endstream' warnings caused by malformed embedded image streams, but these do not affect the extracted text. Marks printed as fractions (e.g. 2½, ½, 1½) are recorded as decimals (2.5, 0.5, 1.5). Several questions in Sections A, B and D depend on diagrams/graphs that are not present in the text layer; these are flagged per question. Non-'OR' compulsory sub-parts (e.g. 17(a)/(b)) are split into separate entries since each can be answered independently; sub-parts sharing an inseparable premise, passage or data (e.g. Q19, Q27, Q28, Q29, Q30) are kept together as one entry with the internal 'OR' retained in the text where present.

questions.text:
Study the sequence of bases in a DNA molecule that is shown below and answer the questions.
5' – GAATTC – 3'
3' – CTTAAG – 5'
(a) What are such sequences called ? Name the enzyme used that recognises such nucleotide sequences.
(b) How do these enzymes function ?

officialAnswer.text:
(a) Palindromic sequences; Restriction endonuclease / EcoRI.
(b) Restriction endonucleases cut the strands of DNA a little away from the centre of the palindrome sites to form sticky ends on each strand / cut at a specific recognition site between two same bases in opposite strands to produce sticky ends / EcoRI cuts the DNA between bases G and A in both strands of the sequence 5’-GAATTC-3’ / 3’-CTTAAG-5’

questions.text:
Given below is a pyramid found in an ecosystem, where each bar represents the standing crop available in the trophic level.
(i) Identify the kind of pyramid and with the help of an example explain the conditions where this kind of pyramid is possible in nature.
(ii) Write any two limitations of ecological pyramids.

officialAnswer.text:
(i) Inverted Pyramid of Biomass. Such pyramids are seen in aquatic conditions where a small standing crop of phytoplankton supports a large standing crop of zooplankton or fish / in a terrestrial ecosystem when a large number of insects feed on a single tree, or any other correct example.
(ii) Ecological pyramids do not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels; they do not accommodate a food web; saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids even though they play a vital role. (Any two)

questions.text: How is Hardy-Weinberg expression (p² + 2pq + q²) = 1 derived ?
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (powers): printed as 'p2'/'q2' without superscript, rebuilt as p²/q²; check against the PDF (confirmed by the marking scheme's own text, which prints p² + 2pq + q²)

officialAnswer.text: According to Hardy-Weinberg principle, the sum total of all allelic frequencies in a population = 1. Let there be two alleles A and a with frequencies ‘p’ and ‘q’; p + q = 1. The frequency of AA will be p² because the probability that allele A with frequency ‘p’ appears on both chromosomes of a diploid individual is the product of probabilities, i.e. p². Similarly the frequency of ‘a’ is q², and Aa is 2pq. Hence p² + 2pq + q² = 1.

questions.text:
A farmer grew two varieties of corn crop in field A and B. He grew normal corn crops in field A and GM corn crops in field B. He observed that corn borers attacked only in field A. To control it, spores of Bt were sprayed on field A.
(a) Name the gene in the spores responsible for control of pest.
(b) What effect will the spores of Bt have on insect pest ?
(c) How has corn plants of field B developed resistance against this pest ? Explain.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) Cry I Ab.
(b) The spores of Bt were mixed with water and sprayed in field A, where these are eaten by the insect larvae; in the gut of the insect, toxins are released and the insect gets killed.
(c) The genetically modified (GM) plants express the Bt gene / produce Bt toxin, which, when ingested, will kill the pest.

questions.text:
Observe the given picture carefully. A mixture of DNA with fragments ranging from 100 base pairs to 1800 base pairs were separated by electrophoresis on agarose gel with the following arrangement :
(a) What result will be obtained in staining with ethidium bromide ? Explain with reasons.
(b) The above setup was modified as shown below and a band with 100 base pairs was obtained at X. What changes were made to the previous design to get a band at ‘X’. Why did the band appear at ‘X’ ?

officialAnswer.text:
(a) No bands will be seen in the agarose gel; DNA fragments, being negatively charged, will not move towards the negative end (cathode) / will remain positioned at the anode (positive end).
(b) Position of the positive terminal (anode) and negative terminal (cathode) has been interchanged. Band at X, being the smallest fragment of DNA, moves farthest towards the anode.

questions.text:
The diagram below shows the distribution of two barnacle species, Chthamalus and Balanus on a rocky sea shore. When Balanus is experimentally removed, Chthamalus expands its range in lower intertidal zone.
(a) Identify and define the ecological phenomenon demonstrated by this observation.
OR
(a) State the principle that explains the elimination of one species.
(b) Two different species can compete for the same resource. Give another example of it.
(c) How do species avoid competition in nature ? Explain with an example.
extractionIssues: Diagram showing distribution of Chthamalus and Balanus barnacle species on the rocky shore (page 17) not reproduced in text layer; the accompanying text description is sufficient to answer the question
Question continues from page 17 to page 19

officialAnswer.text:
(a) Competitive release – a species whose distribution is restricted to a small geographical area due to the presence of a competitively superior species expands its distributional range when the competing superior species is removed.
OR
(a) Gause’s competitive exclusion principle states that two closely related species cannot co-exist indefinitely and the competitively inferior one will be eliminated eventually.
(b) In shallow South American lakes, visiting flamingos and resident fishes compete for common food, Zooplankton / any other correct example.
(c) By “resource partitioning” – they choose different times for feeding or different foraging patterns, e.g. five closely related species of warblers avoid competition and coexist due to behavioural differences in their foraging activities / any other correct example.

(c) What conclusion can you draw from the results of bar graphs of crosses I and II ? Name the genetic principle illustrated.

OR
(a) Monohybrid Cross.
(b) Test Cross – done to find the genotype of an organism showing the dominant phenotype.
(c) It shows that the tall trait is dominant over dwarf. Genetic principle – Law of Dominance.

questions.text: Trace the events from fertilization till implantation of blastocyst in human female. Also mention the site where fertilization takes place.

officialAnswer.text:
After the entry of sperm into the female gamete, it undergoes meiotic division II to produce a haploid ovum (ootid); the nucleus of the sperm and ootid then fuse to form the zygote. The zygote moves through the isthmus of the oviduct towards the uterus and undergoes mitotic division (cleavage) to form blastomeres; the embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is called a morula, which further divides and transforms into a blastocyst. The blastocyst has an outer trophoblast layer and an inner cell mass; the trophoblast attaches to the endometrium, the uterine wall divides rapidly and covers the blastocyst, and it gets embedded in the endometrium – this is called implantation.
The site of fertilization is the ampullary region of the fallopian tube / isthmus-ampullary junction of the fallopian tube.

questions.text:
(i) Case studies of some couples are given below. They were not able to have kids even though the parents were not taking any precautions. They also do not wish to adopt a child or take the help of donors. Study these cases and suggest an appropriate Assisted Reproductive Technology that could help them.
Case I – Female – Normal Reports. Male – Normal sperms but no connection between epididymis and vas deferens.
Case II – Female – Normal eggs but Fallopian tube blocked. Male – Normal sperms. Male reports are normal.
Case III – Female – Normal Reports. Male – Low sperm count with less motility.
(ii) Copper releasing intrauterine devices are very effective and popular contraceptive devices. Name any two copper releasing IUDs. Write two reasons that make them effective contraceptives.

officialAnswer.text:
(i) Case I – In vitro fertilization followed by zygote intra-fallopian transfer (ZIFT) / in vitro fertilization followed by intra-uterine transfer (IUT) / intra-uterine insemination (IUI) / artificial insemination (AI).
Case II – In vitro fertilization followed by IUT.
Case III – Intra-cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) / artificial insemination (AI) / intra-uterine insemination (IUI).
(ii) Copper releasing IUDs are CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375 (Any two). They increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus; Cu ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.

questions.text:
(i) Watson and Crick’s discovery of double helical structure was based on which two findings. Also mention the name of the scientists associated with these findings.
(ii) Write down the salient features of double helix structure of DNA (any three points).

officialAnswer.text:
(i) Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin – X-ray diffraction studies of DNA. Erwin Chargaff – for a double-stranded DNA the ratios between Adenine and Thymine and Guanine and Cytosine are constant and equal to one.
(ii) Salient features: made of two polynucleotide chains with a sugar-phosphate backbone and bases projecting inside; the two chains have antiparallel polarity; bases in the two strands pair through hydrogen bonds – Adenine forms a double hydrogen bond with Thymine and Guanine a triple hydrogen bond with Cytosine; the two chains are coiled in a right-handed fashion, pitch of the helix is 3.4 nm with 10 bp per turn, distance between base pairs ≈ 0.34 nm; the plane of one base pair stacks over the other. (Any three points)

questions.text:

(i) Write the corresponding template strand and m-RNA strand that will be transcribed along with its polarity.
(ii) If GUA of transcribed mRNA is an intron, then depict the sequence involved in formation of mRNA / mature / processed hnRNA strand :
(1) In a bacterium
(2) In humans
(iii) How many amino acids the resulting polypeptide will have after the process of translation in humans ?

officialAnswer.text:

m-RNA: 5' – AUG ACC GUA UUU UCU GUA GUG CCC GUA CUU CAG GCA UUA – 3'
(ii) (1) In a bacterium: 5' – AUG ACC GUA UUU UCU GUA GUG CCC GUA CUU CAG GCA UUA – 3'
(2) In humans: 5' – mGppp AUG ACC UUU UCU GUG CCC CUU CAG GCA UUA – poly A tail 3'

questions.text:
(i) Name the protozoan species that is responsible for causing the most serious and even fatal malarial disease.
(ii) Name the host in which the parasite completes its sexual stages and explain the changes taking place.
(iii) How does the parasite damage the human body after entering the blood stream ?
(iv) Suggest two effective preventive measures to control the spread of this disease in endemic regions.

officialAnswer.text:
(i) Plasmodium falciparum.
(ii) Female Anopheles mosquito. Mosquito picks up gametocytes from the infected person; fertilization and development take place in the mosquito gut; sporozoites from the gut migrate to the salivary glands of the mosquito.
(iii) After entering the blood stream they enter the liver, and then red blood cells, and reproduce asexually; RBCs rupture and a toxic substance, haemozoin, is released, causing chills and high fever.
(iv) Avoiding stagnation of water in and around residential areas; regular cleaning of household coolers; use of mosquito nets; introducing fishes like Gambusia in ponds (they feed on mosquito larvae); spraying insecticides / fitting wire mesh on doors and windows; or any other appropriate preventive measure. (Any two)

questions.text:
(i) What are bio-fertilizers ?
(ii) Name the different types of microorganisms used as bio-fertilizers in organic farming and explain how each contributes to soil fertility.
(iii) Write two advantages of using bio-fertilizers over chemical fertilizers.

officialAnswer.text:
(i) Bio-fertilizers – organisms that enrich the nutrient quality of soil, e.g. bacteria, fungi and cyanobacteria.
(ii) Bacteria / Rhizobium / Azotobacter / Azospirillum – Rhizobium forms a symbiotic association with roots of leguminous plants and fixes atmospheric nitrogen into organic forms for the plant; Azotobacter or Azospirillum fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil. Fungi / genus Glomus – fungi break down organic matter to release nutrients; Glomus forms mycorrhiza with plant roots, helping absorb phosphorus, giving resistance to root-borne pathogens and tolerance to salinity/drought, and increasing plant growth. Cyanobacteria / Anabaena / Nostoc / Oscillatoria (Any one) – fix atmospheric nitrogen, serve as important biofertilizers in paddy fields.
(iii) Do not pollute the environment (soil, ground water); conserve beneficial soil microbes; do not cause contamination or harm human health. (Any two)
